title: Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
detail:
Apple Completes the Set: Every Magnificent Seven Stock Opts Out of OKX-ICE Venue
Decrypt Staff

META
AAPL
MSFT
GOOG
AMZN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Every member of Wall Street's "Magnificent Seven" now wants its stock kept off OKX and ICE's planned tokenized stock venue.

Apple and Meta Platforms are among 11 companies added to the list of objecting issuers in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Thursday.

They join Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia and Tesla, completing a sweep by the group of tech giants that makes up a large share of the S&P 500's value. The other new objectors are Home Depot, Boeing, GE Vernova, Palantir, ServiceNow, S&P Global, KLA, Super Micro Computer and Nebius Group, bringing the total number of companies saying "no" to the OKX and ICE platform to 67.

Meta's objection carries some irony. The Facebook parent once tried to launch its own stablecoin, Libra, later renamed Diem, before abandoning the project in 2022 amid regulatory pushback.

Apple had been one of the last megacaps missing from the list after Amazon, Tesla, and SpaceX objected in the venue's Nov. 2 notice. The tally stood at 56 then, and at nine on Oct. 15, when the first objectors appeared.

Just as notable is who hasn't objected. Crypto-friendly public companies such as Coinbase, Robinhood and Strategy don't appear on the list. Coinbase launched tokenized stocks for non-U.S. users on its Base network in August. Berkshire Hathaway, Visa, and Exxon Mobil are also absent. It's unclear whether OKXICE notified those companies.

Under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act failed to advance in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can't make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC's order. It's worth noting, though, that the objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, plans to offer tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain. An outside "tokenizer" would hold real shares one-for-one through a registered broker-dealer.

With the market's biggest names opted out, it's unclear which major stocks the venue will be able to offer at launch, and its notices don't list the tokens it plans to make available.

Walton Family Gets $100 Billion Richer As Walmart Surges

Five Walton heirs have added $100 billion to their fortunes in 2026, roughly what Oracle's Larry Ellison lost, despite never founding or running a company.

Walmart's stock has climbed 13% this year, outpacing the S&P 500 and dodging the AI sell-off, lifting its market value to $1 trillion.

Alice, Jim, and Rob Walton each gained $28 billion to reach $155 billion, a windfall the author attributes to luck.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

One could say the Walton family does not deserve to be rich. Among the world's wealthiest people, they are the only ones who did not start or serve as senior management of a company, most of which are in the tech industry. Nevertheless, five of Walmart (NYSE: WMT) founder Sam Walton's children and grandchildren have watched their combined net worth rise by $100 billion so far in 2026, Bloomberg reports. That is about the amount Oracle (NASDAQ: ORCL) founder Larry Ellison has lost in the same period.

Sam Walton started Walmart in 1942, at the age of 44. According to the Fortune 500, it was America's largest company for several years, until it yielded that position to Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) last year.

Niloo138 / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

Walmart remains a juggernaut. It employs 2.1 million people ("associates" as the company calls them). In the US, the figure is 1.6 million. Its footprint in its home market is 4,600 Walmart stores and 600 Sam's Club locations. Ninety percent of the US population lives within 10 miles of a Sam's Club or Walmart location.

In the most recent quarter, Walmart revenue rose 5.9% to $187.9 billion. Operating income rose 2.9% to $9.4 billion. John Furner, Walmart's President and CEO, said, "Our team delivered another good quarter, and we continue to make steady progress on the long-term value drivers of our business. Our multi-year growth in eCommerce is evidence that customers are choosing Walmart because we deliver price, speed, and convenience
across a broad assortment. At Walmart, they can have it all."

title: Anthropic's IPO Could Come Within Weeks. Amazon Already Owns a Piece of It.
detail:
Anthropic's IPO Could Come Within Weeks. Amazon Already Owns a Piece of It.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Sat, November 7, 2026 at 9:47 AM CST 5 min read
ANTH.PVT
AMZN
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Anthropic, the AI lab behind the Claude models, has applied to list its stock on the Nasdaq under the symbol "ANT," but its amended filing on Nov. 2 still didn't give a price range.

Financial news service IFR reported last month that Anthropic plans to begin its roadshow (its pitch to big investors) on Nov. 9 and price the deal the next week, citing a person familiar with the process.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) shareholders have a lot riding on how it goes.

Amazon has put $18 billion into Anthropic since 2023, and its balance sheet carried those holdings at about $239 billion on Sept. 30. With Amazon shares at roughly $267 as of this writing, the stake is about 8% of the company's market value.

Still, that $239 billion is Amazon's own estimate. I think what the initial public offering (IPO) gives Amazon investors is a market price to check it against.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

What Amazon owns

The stake has two parts. The first is $8 billion in convertible notes (debt that can become shares) that Amazon bought from 2023 through 2025. Some have already converted, and the others are convertible into around 1.84 billion shares, according to Anthropic's filings.

The second is preferred stock. Amazon put $5 billion in Anthropic's Series G round in the second quarter of 2026. It also agreed to make up to $20 billion more available as it delivers computing capacity, and it spent $5 billion of that on the Series H round.

All told, Amazon owned 164 million preferred shares on Sept. 30, and each converts into 10 shares of nonvoting common stock at an IPO.

But the notes have a cap. Unless Amazon waives it, each note converts only up to the point where Amazon would own 12% of Anthropic's capitalization. Whatever can't convert at the IPO rolls over into future quarters or gets repaid in cash at maturity.

How much is the stake worth?

Amazon carried its preferred stock at $14.8 billion at the end of 2025 and at $92.5 billion on Sept. 30, while the value of its notes climbed to $146.2 billion from $45.8 billion. Together, the two came to around $239 billion, almost four times the year-end figure. But the two parts got there differently. The preferred stock was already at $92.5 billion on June 30, when the notes were at $97.9 billion.

title: CoreWeave’s Bonds Now Yield More Than 16%, Days Before Earnings
detail:
CoreWeave’s Bonds Now Yield More Than 16%, Days Before Earnings
Omor Ibne Ehsan

CRWV
MSFT
NVDA
AMZN
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Quick Read

CoreWeave's 2032 bond yields over 16% against a 10% coupon, signaling lenders doubt it can keep refinancing before its November 10 earnings.

Microsoft supplied roughly 67% of CoreWeave's 2025 revenue, while it winds down an Oracle rental deal and trims its smaller neocloud suppliers.

Credit stress is rising at NVIDIA and Amazon too, yet levels remain low, so the strain stays concentrated on the weakest borrower.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

On November 6, 2026, the 2032 bond of CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) traded at a yield above 16%, even though it pays a coupon of only 9.625%. Lenders usually ask for that kind of return only when they doubt a company can keep refinancing.

24/7 Wall St.

The bond move followed a jump in the cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt. A credit default swap works like an insurance policy: the buyer pays an annual premium and collects if the borrower defaults. Five-year protection rose above 1,289 basis points on November 5, which works out to an annual premium of about 12.9% of the debt insured. It then fell about 8% to around 1,155 basis points on November 6.

The stock moved in the opposite direction. Shares fell 9.83% on November 5 to $43.66, then traded at $46.40 late on November 6, up 6.28%. That bounce had no clear link to the bond market.

Third-quarter results are scheduled for November 10 after the close. Right now, bondholders and stock analysts are pricing two very different companies, and that report is the first real test of which group is right.

Why a 16% Yield Raises Borrowing Costs

A bond that yields far more than its coupon trades well below face value, because buyers will hold it only at a discount large enough to lift their return. In mid-October, the $1.25 billion issue traded at 15% and closed at 14.5%. It now yields more than it did then.

title: Dan Ives: Big Tech Free Cash Flow “Will Trough in 1H2027” as Capex Growth Peaks Early
detail:
Dan Ives: Big Tech Free Cash Flow “Will Trough in 1H2027” as Capex Growth Peaks Early
Gian Estrada

AMZN
META
MSFT
GOOG

Trading disclosure
Dan Ives: Big Tech Free Cash Flow "Will Trough in 1H2027" as Capex Growth Peaks Early ©da-kuk from Getty Images Signature and CG6 Images from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. now expects Big Tech's capex growth to peak in 2027, and free cash flow at Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet and Amazon to bottom in the first half of that year.

Analysts' consensus for Microsoft already shows the trough and rebound Ives describes.

Amazon and Meta are deeper in the hole: Meta's third-quarter capex outran its operating cash, and Amazon's free cash flow, on TIKR's measure, fell to $7.7 billion in 2025.

Ives has the bottom about right, but the full payoff still looks like a 2029 story.

Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. now thinks the cash squeeze at Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ), Alphabet (GOOG) and Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) will end sooner than he expected.

In a post on X on Nov. 5, he wrote that "Big Tech capex growth rate now peaks in 2027 vs our previous view that would not happen until 2028/2029." He pointed to the midterm results, especially in Texas, where he expects the data center buildout to slow.

In a follow-up, he tied it to cash: "Free cash flow will trough in 1H2027 and starting in the 2H of next year will start to show a trajectory towards a major rebound in 2028 and massive FCF ramp in 2029-2030."

Bloomberg Intelligence's Mandeep Singh put a number on it. On the Bloomberg Intelligence podcast on Nov. 4, he pointed to Texas data centers and said: "2027 capex could be revised lower by 5 to 7%."

Microsoft's Numbers Already Look Like This

Microsoft's fiscal year ends in June, so its fiscal 2027 includes the first half of 2027, where Ives puts the trough. Analysts expect free cash flow to fall to $34.0 billion that year, about half of fiscal 2026's $67.0 billion, then rebound to $52.3 billion in fiscal 2028.

MSFT Free Cash Flow, Actual and Consensus Estimates: Fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

Microsoft's free cash flow already fell to $18.6 billion in its September quarter from $25.7 billion a year earlier, and a day after that report it sold $25 billion of bonds, its first US investment-grade sale since 2017.

Microsoft was the only one of the five biggest hyperscalers, counting Oracle, whose free cash flow stayed positive in the third quarter.

Amazon and Meta Have the Deeper Hole

On TIKR's measure, Amazon's free cash flow fell to $7.7 billion in 2025, from $32.9 billion in 2024.

AMZN Free Cash Flow: 2021-2025 (TIKR)

Meta's purchases of property and equipment nearly doubled to $69.7 billion in 2025, from $37.3 billion.

META Capital Expenditures: 2021-2025 (TIKR)

Meta's third-quarter capex, including finance-lease principal payments, rose 80% to $34.9 billion, more than the $32.8 billion its operations brought in, and on Oct. 26 it said it plans to sell up to $95 billion of stock. Alphabet burned $9.07 billion of cash in the quarter, according to Reuters.

title: 3 Internet Giants to Hold for the Next 10 Years
detail:
3 Internet Giants to Hold for the Next 10 Years
John Ballard, The Motley Fool
Sat, November 7, 2026 at 5:35 AM CST 5 min read
GOOG
^IXIC
AMZN
NVDA
NFLX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX: ^IXIC) is down about 5% since the end of September, as of Nov. 2, 2026. The sell-off comes as Wall Street worries about big tech's spending on artificial intelligence (AI). But leading tech stocks remain some of the best ways to build wealth over the long term.

Over the last 10 years, Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), and Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX) each grew revenue at least fivefold, and hundreds of millions of people use their services daily. Each is benefiting from AI, making them three of the best internet giants to hold for the next 10 years. Here's why they are worth buying now for the long term.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
1. Alphabet

Alphabet runs Google Search and YouTube, and its Gemini app just hit 1 billion users. Yet the stock is down 19% since Sept. 30, trailing the Nasdaq. That dip could be an opportunity, since fears that AI chatbots will replace Google may be overblown.

AI is actually helping Alphabet grow Search ad revenue. During the third-quarter earnings call, CEO Sundar Pichai said query growth is the fastest in five years, partly driven by increasing usage of AI Mode, Google's chatbot-style search feature. Now Google is rolling out AI Mode ads globally, giving it more search queries to monetize.

Growing usage of AI features helped push Search revenue up 12% year over year to $63 billion last quarter. Pichai said the trust Google has built "with scale in billions of users" will "end up being a huge differentiator" in AI.

One risk is that AI Mode ads currently earn less per search, which management said weighed on results. Still, the stock looks reasonably priced at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of about 18 times 2027 earnings estimates, below its five-year average trailing P/E of about 24, and analysts expect about 17% annual earnings growth over the next five years.

2. Amazon

Amazon leads online shopping with hundreds of millions of Prime members and also leads the cloud computing market with Amazon Web Services (AWS). The stock is down just 0.9% since Sept. 30 and up 7% year-to-date as of Nov. 2.

AI is a big opportunity for these businesses. More than 400 million customers used Alexa for Shopping, Amazon's agentic AI assistant, in the past year, and U.S. users spend 50% more per order. In AWS, revenue commitments for its Graviton and Trainium chips each rose more than 20 times year over year, and customers using them saved more than $2 billion last quarter. Those savings are why companies stick with AWS.
